node_title: Death Whispers in a Cat's Ear

checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The opening bedroom sequence and the mod-hub scene deliver real texture pull — the helix zipper pull, the Saltline foil animation, Inés's fern-light tattoos, the amber Thread pods — but the back half becomes a dense procedural of office paperwork, filing, invoices, and case-closing logistics that observes GLMZ's bureaucracy and horror mechanics without offering comparable sensory seduction.
checks.Fix: Cut or compress the Rennick-office administrative stretch and redistribute its page-weight toward more strange-beautiful GLMZ texture (the flood-channel algae glow, the Thread pods, the mod-hub's living light) so allure keeps pace with the procedural horror throughout, not just in the first third.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The story opens directly into Celeste's emotionally loaded bedroom scene—memory objects, a dead ex-boyfriend's hologram, packing to run away with a possibly-sinister voice—immediately demanding plot and backstory investment rather than a grounded, low-stakes entry beat of ordinary world-functioning.
checks.Fix: Precede this scene with a brief grounded moment—a commute, a transaction, an ordinary city routine observed by someone jaded to it—before dropping into Celeste's charged, plot-heavy departure.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: The bare acronym 'GLMZ' is used with an in-line gloss ('Great Lakes Metropolitan Zone — GLMZ on every form') which is fine, but 'E.L.F.' appears multiple times (e.g., 'The E.L.F. is absent from it') with no expansion anywhere in the text, and 'CorpoNation' is used as if self-explanatory without ever being unpacked as an acronym or term for a first-time reader.
checks.Fix: Add an in-voice gloss the first time E.L.F. appears, such as 'the Emergent Lattice Fragment—E.L.F. in Arcturus's own shorthand—' before any subsequent bare use of the acronym.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The moment tracing the helix zipper-pull — remembering watching Jace trace the same spiral on his wrist 'from the front row' and later using it herself to catch his overwhelm, then her fingers catching in the zipper track and her refusal to force it because 'force is exactly what she can't spend on the one thing she has left of him' — gives a small, specific, human crack beneath the tactical/functional scenes.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The final beat—Rennick setting a second chair for a new, cold-walk-in client while feeling 'a cold seam running against the grain of the Network's steady weight' moving up the stairs with her—resolves nothing; it reopens the case's engine on a new victim, landing exactly one beat past the paperwork/payout handoff that closed the Hartley file.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The zipper-pull helix that Cel struggles with when packing reads first-pass as a poignant object of grief; on a reread, its jam ('the harder she pulls the deeper it seats... force is exactly what she can't spend on the one thing she has left of him') mirrors the story's central irony that the voice she can't let go of is precisely the thing endangering her, and the closing Andersonville scene's 'half a degree off' cadence retroactively re-colors every earlier moment she overrides her own instinct to name the wrongness.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The Celeste thread reads as a tuned, gateway-accessible scene—but the elided middle collapses into an ensemble procedural (Rennick, Tamsin, Corvin, Analog, Aleksei, Douglas, Mei-Lin) stacked with dense, unexplained lore (Meridian, Arcturus, the Tributary, Scatter, E.L.F., Aleksei's compute-lease chain, Feliksas's shadow log) dropped on a first-time reader with almost no orientation, which reads like the invested-reader version left structurally intact rather than a targeted new-reader pass.
checks.Fix: Add brief grounding beats (a clause or short aside) when introducing each new faction/term (Meridian, the Tributary, Arcturus OC unit, the Scatter/E.L.F.) so a first-time reader can track who's who without needing prior installment knowledge, without restructuring the ensemble scenes themselves.
